chunks: By Allah, I did not conceal a small amount,
nor did I tell a lie,
and I had been informed of this station and this day.
Beware that sins are like unruly horses upon which their riders have been placed,
and their reins have been let loose, so that they would jump with them into the Hellfire.

key_terms.خَيْلٌ شُمُسٌ: Unruly horses (specifically those that throw off their reins)
key_terms.وَشْمَة: A small amount or a little bit

ai.seo_question: What is the metaphor used in Nahj al-Balagha to describe the nature of sins?
ai.summary: Delivered during the pivotal moment of allegiance in Medina, this saying underscores Imam Ali’s (AS) self-authentication as the divinely appointed successor, emphasizing his absolute integrity against potential accusations of concealment. The metaphor of 'unbridled horses' vividly illustrates how sins, once their reins are loosened, carry their owners uncontrollably into the Fire, a concept deeply resonant with Shia teachings on the autonomous power of habitual sin to lead the soul astray.

en.sayed-ali-raza: By Allāh, I have not concealed a single word
and I had been informed of this event and of this time.
Beware that sins are like unruly horses on whom their riders have been placed
and their reins have been let loose so that they would jump with them in Hell.
